extracted.intended_audience: students, critics, and practitioners of humor (humorists, comedy writers, literary scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: A theoretical account of what humor is, how jokes are structured, and the psychological/social sources that make jokes succeed or fail; aimed to guide analysis and creation of humorous material. Focuses on play-attitude, joke mechanics (negative/positive currents and the 'point'), audience impulses, and cultural/contextual constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: play_attitude (play as basis of humor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Play, then, is a preliminary or divertive surface-life in which success is fun, but failure funny. Humor is conceived and bred to flourish in the attitude of play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor requires a playful stance: the audience and performer must treat the situation as a form of play so that failures can be enjoyed rather than agonized over. In non-play contexts the same incidents may not be funny. Example: children laugh indiscriminately because their play-attitude is nearer to true purpose of humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: humor_as_defensive_instinct (shock-absorber)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor operates as a ‘very inward indispensable little shock-absorber — an instinct ... for making the best of a bad thing.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good humorous writing or performance often reframes or mitigates disappointment or pain into amusement. Effective humor preserves the audience's 'digestion' by softening irritations. Anti-pattern: treating setbacks solely as tragedy rather than finding the mitigating twist.

rubrics_metrics.name: pathos_element (humor contains potential tears)
rubrics_metrics.description: In every case in which a man laughs humorously there is an element which, if his sensitivity were sufficiently exaggerated, would contain the possibility of tears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong humor is often grounded in genuine loss, failure, or suffering; the presence of a poignantly close counterfactual increases the comic effect. Avoid purely flippant jokes that lack any hint of real stake when a deeper, bittersweet tone is intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: comic_agility (welcome of void)
rubrics_metrics.description: The true agility of his comic sense is proven ... in the alert twinkle of welcome with which he greets any genuine and definite void appearing where a pleasure was expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A skilled humorist responds to disappointments or voids with an immediate appreciative perspective; comedic timing and the performer's attitude toward failure are crucial. Example: the tack/thumb anecdote — smiling at a thwarted intended pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: the_point_of_a_joke (coincidence_of_negative_and_positive)
rubrics_metrics.description: A joke is a little node ... created by the exact coincidence of a playful shock or disappointment with a playful or a genuine satisfaction. We call this fine moment of co-identity the 'point' of a joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful jokes engineer a tight coincidence between an expectation being thwarted (negative) and an unexpected gratification (positive). Crafting the 'point' — the pivot where the two currents meet — is the central technical task in joke-writing. Anti-pattern: weak or muddy payoff where the coincidence is unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: negative_and_positive_currents (structure_of_humor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor ... possesses two currents — a negative (a discommoding of some light or playful interest) and a positive (a gratification of some interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing a joke, explicitly identify what will supply the negative current (the aroused expectation or thwarting) and the positive current (the assumed or explicit gratification). Balance them; the interplay produces the laugh. Failure modes include not arousing interest or arousing an inappropriately serious interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: proportion_and_targeting_of_interests
rubrics_metrics.description: One may fail to arouse any interest ... or he may arouse a too serious interest ... or perhaps an interest badly proportioned to that which is to supply the positive current; ... he may have miscalculated on the positive side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective humor requires proportioning the magnitude and seriousness of the led-up expectation to the scale of the punch/relief. Misproportion leads to jokes that miss fire or provoke hostility. Test material on intended audience to check proportionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: contextual_specificity_and_fragility_of_jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: A joke is not a thing to be mauled and tinkered ... from one nation, race, tribe, family, generation, or language, into another. It is a chemical gem, a delicate and precarious contexture of non-affinitive qualities ... Every jest has its season; it flourishes and dies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jokes are often culture-, situation-, and relationship-specific (inside jokes). When reusing material, adapt for local expectations and shared knowledge; literal translation often flattens the joke. Antipattern: transplanting literal jokes across cultures/languages without recalibrating.

rubrics_metrics.name: audience_common_impulses (play upon shared_appetites)
rubrics_metrics.description: For humorists ... it is necessary to play upon impulses that are common at least to a considerable group, and can be relied upon to be in a state of appetite almost all the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target impulses or motifs widely shared by the intended audience (e.g., vanity, hunger for truth, social habits). Inside domestic humor works because cohabitants share triggers; public humor should rely on broader, dependable appetites. Avoid hyper-personal references with unfamiliar audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: humor_and_hostility (ridicule_as_a_source)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the impulses ... is the impulse to fight. ... philosophers have been informing the world that the essence of humor is ridicule, that laughter is always at somebody ... 'sudden glory' and 'feeling of superiority.' Ridicule is a fine weapon; derisive humor is a social corrective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derisive or satiric humor leverages feelings of superiority/sudden glory and can function as social critique. Use with care: it’s potent but can wound; its success often depends on shared sympathy or prior frustration. Anti-pattern: indiscriminate scorn that alienates the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: complex_emotional_process (joke_not_single_feeling)
rubrics_metrics.description: A joke is not a single feeling; it is an emotional process. The thing that makes a person whom we scorn comic, and not merely contemptible, is that our scorn enters into that process at a point where we ourselves have just been baffled and deprived of some other satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the layered emotions in a joke: sympathy, deprivation, scorn, relief. Skilled humor arranges these so the audience experiences a composite pleasure. Avoid one-note attacks that lack the interplay of feelings.

rubrics_metrics.name: sexual_implication_as_humor_source
rubrics_metrics.description: Another passion ... that is at least equal ... is the passion of sex. ... the swift sharp force with which these imprisoned hungers will seize upon any least gap or stumbling of speech or idea ... is the one thing upon which every humorist in every company can rely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sexual innuendo and implication are ready reliable sources of comic positive current, especially where repression creates hunger. Cultural/contextual sensitivity is critical: some cultures/audiences prefer overt Rabelaisian license, others prefer furtive implication. Anti-pattern: lazy 'naughty kitten' jokes that exploit sexual hints without craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: truth_as_source_of_humor
rubrics_metrics.description: We are always hungry for the simple truth. ... place Truth herself beside sex and sudden glory as a chief source of the joy motive in popular jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revealing or pointing to simple, overlooked truths—incongruities between claim and reality—can generate laughs. Use truthful insight to create satisfaction that counts as the positive current. Distinguish this from mere glee or cruelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: distinction_between_humor_and_glee
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not humor, but glee, that makes them whoop so loud at cruel gibes and obscene quips ... Glee ... is of no more special pertinence to the art of joking than any other pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor (subtler emotional process combining play and insight) should be distinguished from mere glee (raw delight in cruelty or obscenity). For craftful humor, avoid relying only on shock/glee; aim for the processual 'point' instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: flexibility_vs_fixation (humor_independent_of_belief)
rubrics_metrics.description: Its essence is flexibility instead of fixation. ... Not only is humor independent of any particular belief or intellectual commitment, but in softening the rigor of the passions it removes the chief obstacle to the process of verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor benefits from an open, flexible stance toward ideas; it should welcome arriving truths and accommodate them. Avoid dogmatic or rigid positioning that prevents playful reappraisal; the comedic voice often thrives on intellectual hospitality.
